subject: Predicting Detection Probability for Continuous Covariates

messages.author: 67eefb0e32c64fae
messages.subject: Predicting Detection Probability for Continuous Covariates
parts:
Hi there! I am looking to predict detection probability over a range of dayscores (the day each survey was conducted on). Dayscores range from 8 to 122, and there are 294 obsCovs slots, some of which are NA.

I keep running into errors saying that I do not have the appropriate number of rows. I suspect that my formatting of the data frame in newdata.5 is to blame.

#Dynamic Model (DP is a function of Dayscore (May 15th))
  fm5 <- colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~unlist(obs.dayscore), data = FosnUMF, se = TRUE)
  range(obs.dayscore, na.rm = TRUE)
  newdata.5 <- data.frame(Dayscore = data.frame(obs.dayscore))
  newdata.5
  fm5.ds <- predict(fm5, newdata=newdata.5, type="det", appendData=TRUE)

Error in data.frame(out, as(newdata, "data.frame")) : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 190, 21
In addition: Warning message:
'newdata' had 21 rows but variables found have 294 rows 

Any help would be appreciated! :)

Sean

messages.subject: Re: Predicting Detection Probability for Continuous Covariates
parts:
Hello - I have continued to pursue this error to no avail. The issue appears to be linked to how predict() interprets my data frame of Dayscores. The dataframe is 21 rows (sites) by 14 columns (site visits), and the warning message I get below keeps mentioning the dimensions of this data frame. So I don't think it knows how to treat the Dayscore variable as a set of continuous values.

I have set Dayscore up as the following:

obs.dayscore <- data.frame(FosnEH[,45:58]) #Dayscore of Visit

#Create UMF (also combines obs.Covs)
FosnUMF <- unmarkedMultFrame(y = y, siteCovs = site.covs, obsCovs = list(obs.visit=obs.visit,obs.dayscore=obs.dayscore,obs.date=obs.date,obs.effort=obs.effort), numPrimary = T, yearlySiteCovs = years.cov)

Then I try to model it:

#Dynamic Model (DP is a function of Dayscore (May 15th))
  fm5 <- colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~unlist(obs.dayscore), data = FosnUMF, se = TRUE)

Warning message:
'newdata' had 122 rows but variables found have 21 rows

messages.author: 67eefb0e32c64fae
messages.subject: Re: Predicting Detection Probability for Continuous Covariates
parts: Once again - persistence prevails! The solution: You MUST name your "newdata" data frame contents the SAME as the covariates in your model.
#Dynamic Model (DP is a function of Dayscore (May 15th))

fm5 <- colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~obs.dayscore, data = FosnUMF, se = TRUE)
  newdata.5 <- data.frame(obs.dayscore = seq(8, 122, by = 1))
fm5.ds <- predict(fm5, newdata=newdata.5, type="det", appendData=TRUE)
